correctness.rationale: The exact law follows from strict chord endpoint alternation and two equally offset supporting-line equations; all boundaries are explicitly included. Improper Riemann sums cover 0<q<1, harmonic summation covers q=1, and dominated series convergence gives the Hurwitz-zeta constants for q>1. A uniform sine-quotient error controls the moving exponent. At rare-tail jump points, strict sine-over-argument monotonicity ensures correct inclusion. Independent Cartesian computations pass 18,660 finite checks; they are corroborative rather than substitutes for proofs.

value.rationale: The precise location of intersections formed by congruent diagonals is a natural metric refinement of current equal-diagonal polygon dissections. The theorem reveals a bulk Pareto law with infinite mean and a distinct lattice-controlled rare-event phase, an exact three-regime moment spectrum with a compact-uniform critical window, and parity-dependent near-diameter contact thresholds. These parameters are intrinsic (distance from diametral span, radius, moment order) and the resulting all-parity classification is more than a routine point estimate.
